facts.text: Apple is about to launch its next entirely new product, according to reports.

Apple launched that new version of Siri – which uses artificial intelligence and an understanding of everything on a person's phone to provide more useful answers – with the release of iOS 27 and its other software updates earlier this month.

During that reveal, Apple showed off new designs for its StandBy mode – intended to work as an ambient display, and launched when the foldable phone is sat on a surface like a tent – and the home hub may have similar features including new clocks and data.
Apple is also working on improving its smart home ecosystem, Bloomberg reported.
That will include a new software framework to control other devices, working with third-party manufacturers to make smart home accessories that work with Siri.
While Apple has long been rumoured to be working on such new products and upgrades, it is believed that the introduction of that new Siri has held them back.
Apple has been resistant to launching the products without a satisfactory version of the virtual assistant to run on them, rumours have suggested.
Apple hopes that people will put a number of the devices around their house.
They could be used to control smart devices, communicate between different home hubs, play music and look through photos, Bloomberg suggested.
It will use the existing visual style of Siri, for instance, and a home screen that borrows from the iPad's app designs and the Apple Watch 's icons, as well as the iPhone's widgets.
Apple ’s new iPhone Air could be a hint at the future of the company’s devices, according to a new report.
From reproductive rights to climate change to Big Tech, The Independent is on the ground when the story is developing.
And unlike many other quality news outlets, we choose not to lock Americans out of our reporting and analysis with paywalls.
We believe quality journalism should be available to everyone, paid for by those who can afford it.
The iPhone Air is the thinnest iPhone that Apple has ever made, at 5.6mm.
When it was launched, earlier this month, the company said it was a step towards its vision of an iPhone that is simply a flat piece of glass.
Apple is planning to launch the foldable phone in 2026, multiple reports have suggested.
It could come alongside the other, more traditional devices on their usual September release schedule, rumours have indicated.
Many of Apple’s competitors, such as Google and Samsung, have already launched similar devices.
